updateTaskPriority(id, p) · setDueDate(id, d) · addTag(id, tag)
getTask returns Optional — absence is a value, not a null ✓
honest: addObserver is NOT on the interface, so a different
TaskService impl silently loses observer support
fix: hoist addObserver / removeObserver onto TaskService
createTask → put, then notify with oldStatus = null (a birth event)
notify ONLY if old != new → no spam on idempotent updates
requireTask(id) → throws on an unknown id instead of a silent no-op
notifyObservers: COPY the list under the lock, then iterate OUTSIDE it
→ a slow listener can't block registration, and a listener that
registers another listener can't deadlock or throw CME ✓
honest: observers run on the CALLER's thread — a slow or
throwing listener still delays / breaks the caller
honest: every query is an O(n) full scan — no secondary index
on assignee, status or tag. Fine for a board, not for a tenant-wide search.
upgrade: Map<assigneeId, Set<taskId>> kept in step with writes,
or hand the whole query problem to a real index
deleteTask removes from the map only — no tombstone, no event fired
THE MODEL — the entity guards its own lifecycle
DONE → stamp completedAt; anything else → CLEAR it
read-old + write-new in ONE critical section
honest: only status is synchronized — title, priority,
dueDate and assignee are plain unguarded setters
the rules live on the ENUM, as EnumSets — one
readable place, and every caller inherits them ✓
self-transition is always allowed → idempotent PATCHes
the error message even lists allowedNext() — debuggable by design
ONE method — assignee mailer, activity feed and
burndown chart all plug in without touching the service
honest: no onAssigned / onDeleted — only status moves are observable
User (+ UserRole, teamIds, active) · Team · Comment
honest: User / Team / Comment exist in model/ but
TaskService has no API for them — assignee is a raw String id
say this out loud: modelled, not wired up
THE OBSERVER PATH — one status change, three side effects
copy the list under the lock
activity feed — appends an audit line
burndown chart — recounts the DONE column
The subject never learns what a listener does — that is the entire value of Observer here.
Adding "post to Slack" is a new class and one addObserver call; InMemoryTaskService is not edited.
The ceiling: it is a synchronous in-process fan-out. One listener throwing kills the whole notify loop
and the caller sees the exception. Production answer: try/catch per listener, then an event queue.
